text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- (IU leader) Anguita asks PSOE to write down its offer
- Archbishops of Avila and Murcia want their own universities
- An opinion poll show majority is in favor of (former head of Socialist Party) Gonzalez's decision (of not seeking reelection as leader of the party).
- Judge does not request measures against (Sogecable's chairman) Polanco.
EL MUNDO
- (New head of Socialist Party) Almunia asks unions and non-governmental organizations for help to replace the right in power
- 'Zamora' committe (investigatingr possible illicit financing of the PP) dissolved.
- (PM) Aznar offered (Guinea's) Obiang to review the asylum granted by Spain to Severo Moto.
- Obesity is caused by a gene, which prevents knowing when it's time to stop eating
LA VANGUARDIA
- Women's wages one third lower than men's.
CINCO DIAS
- Tolerance in allowing new firms to be listed - from yesterday a new order make things easier to enter the Bourse.
- Santander out of the Bodegas Riojanas' capital after the sale of 40 percent of the shares for 2 billion pesetas.
- (Economy Minister) Rodrigo Rato asks for lower wages to save 100 billion pesetas (in pensions and wages to civil servants).
- Motorway tolls to fall nine percent from September
EXPANSION
- (Market watchdog) CNMV close to who got profit from Endesa's bid
- Bourse above 590, boosted by banks
- Prima Inmobiliaria wants its relaunch, to workl on 25 billion pesetas capital increase
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- (Telefonica's chairman) Villalonga finlises the changes in the board. Tomorrow it should appoint three new general directors and a general secretary.
- CNMV investigates Banco Santander de Negocios and Goldman officials for the Sevillana acquisition
